fact: The MINFOPRA-KOICA steering committee, meeting on 20 August 2026, reviewed a project launched in 2024 to build civil servants' digital skills through e-government tools, including Smart Campus sites at four institutions and the design documents and training plans for a Learning Management System for continuing training of public agents.
system: Projet d'accélération de la sensibilisation numérique et du renforcement des capacités (MINFOPRA-KOICA)

fact: Cameroon's government launched the online platform train.patnucelearning.cm on 21 September 2026 under PATNUC to train a target of 15,000 civil servants and public-enterprise staff in digital skills, with registration opened that day.
The programme is stated to be open to agents of all ministries, including deconcentrated services, and to staff of public establishments and enterprises.
Le Financier d'Afrique reports that an online learning platform was announced to train 15,000 public agents in artificial intelligence, blockchain and digital transformation.
The E-GovA 2026 programme presented on 1 October at the Minpostel includes training workshops for public agents, held 14-17 October 2026 in Yaounde.

PATNUC (MINPOSTEL, World Bank-financed) published on 2026-04-28 the ranking of consultants shortlisted to deliver digital-transformation training and capacity building for public agents through an e-learning platform, with the Groupement ITS et Umbrella first on 90/100 and invited to negotiate.
system: PATNUC e-learning training for public agents

fact: MINADER reports that PATNUC has launched a training programme open to agents of the various public administrations nationwide, with five certifying online modules (including AI, LLM and blockchain) and registrations open; no number trained is given.
